DynamicCodeSegment.description:
Describes one dynamically generated code region that executed.

Dynamic code segments are added when execution reaches memory previously
registered as dynamic code (for example after VirtualAlloc/WriteProcessMemory
style paths).

This section is useful for unpacking and staged payload detection.

tag.description:
Memory-map tag assigned to the dynamic region.

Tags help correlate the segment with allocation provenance in traces.
tag.title: Tag

base.description:
Base address of the dynamic code region.

Use this with memory layout data to inspect surrounding mapped content.
base.title: Base

size.description:
Region size of the dynamic code segment.

Large regions may indicate unpacked module images or staged blobs.

EntryPoint.description:
Represents one emulation execution primitive captured as a run.

A run may be a module entry point, callback, exported function, injected
thread, or other execution start context.

Most behavioral telemetry is attached at this level, so treat each entry as
a self-contained execution narrative.

type.description:
Kind of code that this run executes.

Examples include the module entry point, an export, a TLS callback, and a thread.

name.description:
Detail for ``type``, or null when the type has no detail.

For example the export name, the TLS callback index, the dependency module, or the IRP major function.
name.title: Name

start_address.description:
Address where this run began executing.

Use this as the anchor when following control flow in disassembly.
start_address.title: Start Address

args.description: Argument values supplied at run entry.
args.title: Args

pid.description:
Process identifier associated with the run context.

Populated when process context is known for this entry point.
pid.title: Pid

tid.description:
Thread identifier associated with the run context.

Useful for correlating with per-event ``pos.tid`` values.
tid.title: Tid

instruction_count.description:
Instruction count executed for this run.

Can be limited by configuration caps or early termination conditions.
instruction_count.title: Instruction Count

api_hash.description:
SHA-256 hash over unique API names invoked in first-seen order.

Use this for coarse behavioral clustering across samples and architectures.
api_hash.title: Api Hash

return_value.description:
Return value produced when the run ended normally.

Interpret this in the calling convention context of ``type``.
return_value.title: Return Value

error.description:
Run-local error details when execution did not complete cleanly.

Consult this with ``events`` to identify the exact failure transition.

events.description:
Chronological event stream emitted during this run.

Event contents are produced by API, process, file, registry, network, and exception recorders.
events.title: Events

symbol_accesses.description:
Symbol-level access counters observed during tracing.

Present only when memory tracing is enabled in config.
symbol_accesses.title: Symbol Accesses

dynamic_code_segments.description:
Dynamically generated code regions that executed in this run.

Indicates unpacking, JIT-like behavior, or in-memory staging activity.
dynamic_code_segments.title: Dynamic Code Segments

coverage.description:
Sorted list of executed instruction addresses for coverage analysis.

Present only when coverage collection is enabled in config.
coverage.title: Coverage

dropped_files.description:
File artifacts detected as fully written during the run.

Use this list to extract secondary payloads and logs.
dropped_files.title: Dropped Files

memory.description:
Optional memory and module snapshot captured at run completion.

Populate this when memory-layout capture is active for the emulator mode.

EntryPoint.title: EntryPoint

EntryPointType.description: Kind of code that a run executes.

ErrorInfo.description:

explicit runtime limits, or unhandled exceptions.

Inspect this structure first when a run exits unexpectedly.

type.description:
Error category identifier describing the failure mode.

Examples include unsupported API paths, max API limits, and fault conditions raised by emulator hooks. A Python exception in Speakeasy itself, such as a bug in an API handler, is ``internal_error``.

pc.description:
Program counter associated with the error, when available.

Use this address to align failures with disassembly and event traces.
pc.title: Pc

instruction.description:
Faulting instruction text, when known.

Useful for quickly identifying invalid memory operations or bad control flow transitions.
instruction.title: Instruction

address.description: Faulting memory address that triggered the error.
address.title: Address

access_type.description: Memory access type that faulted: read, write, or fetch.

registers.description: Register state snapshot at the time of the error.
registers.title: Registers

stack.description: Stack slots at the time of the error, from the stack pointer up.
stack.title: Stack

pc_module.description: Name of the module that contains the faulting PC, for example ``sample.exe``.
pc_module.title: Pc Module

pc_offset.description: Offset of the faulting PC from the base of ``pc_module``.

address_region.description: Memory region containing the faulting address, if mapped.

nearby_regions.description: Up to 2 nearest memory regions when the faulting address is unmapped.

tid.description: Thread ID at the time of the error.

pid.description: Process ID at the time of the error.
pid.title: Pid

context_summary.description: Human-readable one-line triage summary of the error.
context_summary.title: Context Summary

traceback.description: Python traceback when the error originated from an internal exception.
traceback.title: Traceback

message.description: Text of the Python exception of an ``internal_error``.
message.title: Message

api_name.description: API function name for unsupported-API errors.
api_name.title: Api Name

count.description: API call count that triggered a max-API-count limit.

last_api.description: Last API name invoked before max-API-count termination.

MemoryAccesses.description:
Aggregates read/write/execute counters for one memory region.

These counters are produced by runtime memory tracing hooks when enabled.

Use them to prioritize regions with meaningful behavioral activity.

Total read operations observed for the region.

High read density often indicates lookup tables or parsed structures.

writes.description:
Total write operations observed for the region.

High write density often indicates decoded payload construction.
writes.title: Writes

execs.description:
Total execute operations observed for the region.

Non-zero execution marks code-bearing pages and trampoline regions.

MemoryLayout.description:
Bundles memory-region and loaded-module snapshots for one run.

This object is populated when the emulator captures run-end memory state.

Use it to understand both raw mappings and higher-level module context.

layout.description:
Flat list of captured memory regions for the run.

Entries may include module headers/sections and generic maps.

modules.description:

Use alongside ``layout`` to interpret address ownership and segment roles.

MemoryRegion.description:
Represents one memory layout entry captured for an entry point.

Memory layout capture runs at run completion and may include section-split
module regions plus generic heap/stack mappings.

Use this data to correlate execution artifacts with mapped memory topology.

tag.description:
Region tag assigned by the memory manager.

Tags encode provenance such as module sections, heaps, or emulator internal structures.
tag.title: Tag

base.description:
Base address of the memory region.

Treat this as the start of the region for disassembly and dump slicing.
base.title: Base

size.description:
Region size in bytes.

Combine with ``base`` to derive half-open address ranges.
size.title: Size

perms.description:
Permission string (for example ``r-x`` or ``rw-``).

Interpret this as the final effective page protection at capture time.
perms.title: Perms

is_free.description:
Whether the region had been freed at capture time.

Freed regions can remain visible when memory retention settings keep old maps for analysis.
is_free.title: Is Free

accesses.description:
Optional read/write/execute counters for the region.

Populated primarily when memory tracing was enabled for the run.

data_ref.description:
Optional reference into the top-level report ``data`` store.

When present, resolve this SHA-256 key in ``Report.data`` to recover the compressed region bytes.

StringCollection.description:
Represents one categorized bucket of extracted strings.

String extraction runs both on static image bytes and post-emulation memory
snapshots. This model keeps ANSI and UTF-16 findings separated.

Compare these lists to identify runtime-decoded strings that were not present
in the original file bytes.

ansi.description:
ASCII/ANSI strings extracted for this bucket.

These are populated by static string scans or memory string extraction depending on the parent field.
ansi.title: Ansi

unicode.description:
UTF-16 style strings extracted for this bucket.

Use these to spot wide-character configuration values and command artifacts.
unicode.title: Unicode

StringCollection.title: StringCollection

StringsReport.description:
Groups static and in-memory string extraction results.

Static strings come from the original loaded image, while in-memory strings
are collected after execution and often include decoded/decrypted content.

Use this section to quickly triage embedded versus runtime materialized
indicators.

static.description:
Strings extracted from the initial file image bytes.

Primarily influenced by the module loader and static string scanner.

in_memory.description:
Strings extracted from memory after emulation executes.

Populated when string analysis is enabled and runtime decoding created new string material.

StringsReport.title: StringsReport

SymAccessReport.description:
Summarizes memory accesses to symbol-resolved addresses.

Symbol access accounting is mainly populated when memory tracing is active
and the emulator can resolve touched addresses back to known symbols.

Use these counters to identify import-table walking and export resolution
behavior.

symbol.description:
Resolved symbol name in ``module.symbol`` form.

This identifies the logical target accessed by code during tracing.
symbol.title: Symbol

reads.description:
Number of read accesses observed for this symbol.

High values often indicate lookup loops or pointer chasing.
reads.title: Reads

writes.description:
Number of write accesses observed for this symbol.

Non-zero writes can indicate tampering or patching behavior.
writes.title: Writes

execs.description:
Number of execution accesses observed for this symbol.

Execution hits often represent direct calls/jumps through symbol-backed addresses.

description:
Top-level Speakeasy output report model.

This object combines run telemetry, metadata for the emulated input, and
optional analysis artifacts.

Treat this as the canonical machine-readable output for downstream tooling.

Machine words are ``0x``-prefixed hex strings: addresses, pointers,
handles, raw argument values, return values, register values and exception
codes. A 64-bit word can be above 2**53 or 2**63, and JavaScript, Go
``interface{}``, jq and int64 stores such as SQLite lose such a value as a
JSON number with no error. Quantities, such as sizes, counts, offsets,
ticks and IDs, are JSON numbers.

A key is absent when Speakeasy did not collect its data. An empty list or
object means that Speakeasy collected the data and found nothing.

report_version.description:
Schema/report format version generated by the profiler.

Use this to route parsing logic when consuming multiple report versions.
report_version.title: Report Version

emulation_total_runtime.description:
Total wall-clock runtime in seconds for the emulation session.

Derived from profiler start/stop timing and rounded to milliseconds.
emulation_total_runtime.title: Emulation Total Runtime

timestamp.description:
Epoch timestamp (seconds) captured at emulation start time.

Use this for timeline correlation with external logs.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

arch.description:
Architecture of the input sample, when known.

Populated from loader metadata.

path.description:
Host path of the input file, when the input was loaded from a file.

Useful for provenance tracking in batch pipelines.
path.title: Path

sha256.description:
SHA-256 hash of the emulated input bytes, when available.

Use this as the primary stable sample identifier.
sha256.title: Sha256

size.description:
Input file size in bytes, when available.

Helps validate sample identity and triage packaging anomalies.
size.title: Size

file_type.description:
Kind of input file, when known.

Derived from loader inspection before emulation starts.

image_base.description:
Base address at which the primary module was loaded during emulation.

Use this to rebase analysis tools (e.g. IDA Pro) to match emulated addresses.
image_base.title: Image Base

errors.description:
Top-level emulator errors not tied to a specific run.

These usually reflect session-level failures rather than per-entry-point termination.
errors.title: Errors

strings.description:
Optional static and in-memory string extraction output.

Present only when string analysis is enabled in config.

data.description:
Deduplicated binary payload store keyed by SHA-256.

Resolve ``*_ref`` fields in the report against this mapping to recover compressed payload bytes.
data.title: Data

entry_points.description:
Ordered list of all runs executed during emulation.

This is the primary behavioral timeline for the report.
entry_points.title: Entry Points

title: Report
